supplier_name.description: Name of the supplier who sent this lead

buyer_id.description: Reference to the Buyer record this lead was delivered to (set on sold delivery or by feedback matching)

buyer_record_id.description: Task R1. The Buyer record id, always. buyer_id is overloaded across legacy imports, LeadByte feedback matching and native routing, so it may hold a record id, a buyer_code or a legacy bid. This field is unambiguous. Populated by server/src/lib/buyerIdentity.js. Additive: buyer_id is not redefined and not removed.

buyer_code.description: Task R1. The Buyer.buyer_code, always. Companion to buyer_record_id, kept denormalized so reports can group by the human facing code without a join.

buyer_feedback.description: Latest buyer feedback disposition (from our taxonomy) for this lead, used by reporting

raw_payload.description: JSON string of the original inbound payload

email_normalized.description: Lowercased, trimmed email. The identity match key used by leadbyteWebhook and leadDedupe. Null when the value is absent or not a valid address, so junk never becomes a match key. Written by processLead via src/lib/leadIdentity.js.

mobile_normalized.description: Bare 10-digit US mobile (no country code, no formatting). The identity match key used alongside email_normalized. Null when the number cannot be resolved to a valid NANP number.

email_valid.description: Email deliverability result from the free validation service (format + DNS MX lookup). Runs on the same lead_routes as the HLR lookup.

conv_value.description: Conversion value attributed to this lead

hlr_request.description: JSON string of HLR request body

hlr_status.description: HLR lookup result status e.g. Exact Match

hlr_error.description: HLR error message if lookup failed

leadbyte_request.description: JSON string of payload sent to LeadByte

final_status.description: SUPERSEDED by lead_status. W2-STATUS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D1 and D4. This is the retiring twelve-value enum. It is kept, unchanged, and still dual-written on every live path for the duration of the expand phase, because client/src/**, server/src/functions/webhook.js and server/src/functions/leadbyteWebhook.js still read and write it and are outside W2-STATUS's file ownership. Do not add a new read of this field: read lead_status. It is dropped in the contract release, after W3-UI-STATUS. Never compute money from either field; see is_sold and sale_price_effective.

lead_status.description: W2-STATUS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D1. The canonical operator-facing lead status, exactly seven values. queued: durably saved, not yet settled (covers received, processing, retry-pending, awaiting-cascade). rejected: not accepted as a valid, new, routable lead. disqualified: accepted as valid, then failed a business qualification rule; never offered to a buyer. unsold: qualified, entered distribution, no buyer bought it. sold: at least one valid buyer acceptance. returned: a previously sold lead with an approved return. converted: a previously sold lead confirmed downstream. Precedence when more than one could apply: returned, converted, sold, unsold, disqualified, rejected, queued. That precedence is expressed in server/src/lib/leadStatus.js and is NOT enforced by every live write path; see that module's KNOWN GAP note. Money is never computed from this field.

processing_state.description: W2-STATUS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D1. The internal machine state, deliberately separate from lead_status so a crash can never change a lead's business status. A lead at lead_status queued with processing_state failed is a stuck lead and is the input to the W4-REAPER stuck-lead queue, unless it carries migrated_at.

status_reason.description: W2-STATUS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D1, D3 and D4. Stable machine reason code for the current lead_status, in the SCREAMING_SNAKE convention already used by the routing engine's REASON map and by the code field on every processLead supplier envelope. The three codes the contract names are REJECTED_DNC (D3), REJECTED_DUPLICATE and REJECTED_FAKE (D4). Live paths reuse the existing envelope codes (SOLD, UNSOLD, MISSING_FIELDS, LB_ERROR and the rest) rather than a parallel set. MIGRATED_FROM_PROCESSING, MIGRATED_FROM_QUALIFIED and MIGRATED_FROM_ERROR are written only by the backfill, where the historical row records no machine reason of its own.

status_reason_detail.description: W2-STATUS. Optional human-readable detail behind status_reason, capped at 500 characters. Used for the do-not-contact audit (which field matched and which entry did it, never the raw contact value) and for any other case where the code alone is not enough to act on. Never contains a raw contact value or a credential.

is_qualified.description: W2-STATUS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D4. Derived flag preserving the qualification rate that the retiring Qualified status used to carry, now that Qualified, Processing, Error and Queued all collapse into lead_status queued. TRI-STATE ON PURPOSE: true where the lead provably reached qualification, false where it provably did not, and ABSENT where the row genuinely does not say (a still-processing, queued or errored historical lead). A confident false on an unknowable row would understate the very rate this flag exists to preserve. The backfill reports the size of the unknown bucket.

duplicate_of_lead_id.description: W2-STATUS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D4. The Lead id this lead duplicates, set when lead_status is rejected with status_reason REJECTED_DUPLICATE. Resolved from mapped_fields.merged_into where leadbyteWebhook.js recorded a collapse, otherwise from the oldest non-duplicate lead sharing this lead's normalized email or mobile. Left unset, and reported as a backfill exception, when no original can be identified: never pointed at a guess.

migrated_at.description: W2-STATUS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D4 third risk. Set by the status backfill on every row it migrates. Its purpose is exclusion: a lead carrying this marker reached its current lead_status and processing_state through a migration and not through a live processing run, so it must never be re-driven into live distribution. Thirty code sites treated the retiring Error status as terminal; under D1 those leads become queued and therefore recoverable, and without this marker the first run of any recovery job would flood live distribution with historical failures. server/src/lib/leadStatus.js isExcludedFromRedrive is the single predicate that answers it.

lead_route.description: Additive. The resolved processing route this lead took (standard, gateway, direct, data, event, queue, internal, test). Recorded for reporting and for reading shadow/canary comparisons; the live decision still comes from the inbound payload.

campaign_id.description: Additive. Internal Campaign record id this lead resolved to, from the posted campaign_id when supplied, otherwise matched on vertical. Empty when no campaign matched.

queue_reason.description: Reason the lead was queued for manual handling

trustedform_valid.description: Whether the TrustedForm cert URL passed validation

cert_source.description: Origin of the TrustedForm cert: inbound or backup_store

capi_log.description: JSON list of {connector, event_name, pixel, http_status, fbtrace_id}

delivery_log.description: JSON list of {connector, trigger, http_status, success, error, timestamp} for LeadByteConnector deliveries

delivery_error.description: Summary of any delivery or connector destinations that failed to fire for this lead. Populated from delivery_log. Does not affect final_status.

error_stage.description: Stage where error occurred if any

response_returned.description: JSON string of response sent back to supplier

import_batch_id.description: Batch id stamped on leads created via CSV import, used for filtering and rollback

supplier_payout.description: Supplier payout reported by LeadByte, for true CPL and margin

buyer_conversion.description: Buyer conversion status reported by LeadByte

buyer_returned.description: Whether the buyer returned this lead

buyer_return_reason.description: Reason given for a buyer return

lead_vertical.description: Vertical reported by LeadByte, e.g. MVA

leadbyte_outcome_at.description: When the outcome webhook was received

leadbyte_outcome_payload.description: Full raw JSON of the LeadByte outcome webhook

revenue_source.description: How the revenue value on this lead was determined: leadbyte_buyers, leadbyte_root, direct_route, or unknown. Diagnostic only, does not affect final_status.

is_sold.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once derived flag: true once this lead is ever sold, and never cleared again by any later status change (Returned, Converted, a reprocessed webhook, or a re-run of the backfill in server/src/lib/leadFlags.js). Money must never be computed from final_status/lead_status directly; use this flag instead. Enforced at the database layer by the lead_flags_write_once trigger in server/src/db/schema.js, which silently rejects any UPDATE attempting to move this back to false once it is true.

sold_at.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once. When is_sold first became true, best-effort from processed_at/leadbyte_outcome_at at backfill time. Never rewritten once set.

sale_price_effective.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once. The captured revenue at the moment this lead was first sold. A later conversion or return never changes this value; a later resale-style webhook that tries to overwrite Lead.revenue no longer moves the number actually used for revenue/GP/CPL/ROAS reporting. Null when the lead is sold but no usable revenue value was ever captured (see revenue_source = unknown), which is reported as a distinct backfill exception rather than silently priced at zero.

is_returned.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once derived flag: true once this previously sold lead has an accepted/approved return (final_status = Returned, or an approved ReturnRequest), and never cleared again. is_sold stays true; only this flag distinguishes a return for revenue exclusion (revenue = sum of sale_price_effective where is_sold and not is_returned).

returned_at.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once. When is_returned first became true. Never rewritten once set.

is_converted.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once derived flag: true once this previously sold lead is confirmed downstream by the buyer (final_status = Converted), and never cleared again. Does not change is_sold or sale_price_effective, which keep reporting the original sale.

converted_at.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once. When is_converted first became true. Never rewritten once set.

conversion_type.description: W1-FLAGS, forge-pack/CONTRACT.md D2. Immutable, write-once. The buyer's conversion disposition (from buyer_conversion, e.g. signed/retained), or 'converted' when no disposition detail was captured. Never rewritten once set.
